messages:
maya: quick heads-up — i'm doing a short spike on collector topology choices for telemetry routing. we need to decide between a gateway-led fanout (single ingress -> split per-signal/tenant) vs a multiplexed agent (edge agent holds routing and minor filtering). thoughts? :thinking:
ian: +1 for capturing pros/cons early. what are our primary constraints? latency, retention cost, and operational surface area for customers?
sophia: curious — do we expect heavy per-tenant exporter variance? if many tenants want different exporters/retentions we might prefer per-tenant pipelines at the gateway to avoid shipping raw spans around.
tom: latency sensitive traces prefer agent-side keep/drop decisions so we avoid roundtrip to gateway for basic sampling. but agent-side logic increases upgrade/compat complexity.
alex: note: we also have quotas and per-api-route throttles in console; if gateways centralize routing we can enforce quotas more easily. single control plane is easier for rollouts.
maya: agree. i'm weighing: 1) gateway fanout -> simpler agent, centralized enforcement, potential network egress/ingest spike; 2) intelligent agent multiplex -> reduces egress, faster local sampling but heavier agent upgrades and config sync.
ian: can we do hybrid? e.g., agent does coarse sampling + tenant tagging, gateway applies per-tenant exporter selection and retention policies. reduces raw volume but keeps central controls.
sophia: hybrid seems pragmatic for transitional phase. downside: double-hop decisions may cause uneven attribute enrichment unless we standardize normalization at agent.
tom: example config snippet i'm imagining for gateway pipelines (pseudo):
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols: grpc/http
processors:
  batch:
  resource/tenant-normalizer:
exporters:
  tenant-a-s3:
  tenant-b-stdout:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces/tenant-a:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource/tenant-normalizer, batch]
      exporters: [tenant-a-s3]
```
alex: that looks good. question: who owns per-tenant retention lifecycle? product or infra? i think product defines retention policy, infra implements and enforces.
maya: product defines, infra implements — agreed. but thx, decision impacts our rollout UX in console: if gateway-level pipelines are required, console needs a "exporter wiring" UI to configure exporters per-tenant. more work.
ian: operational concerns: gateway fanout increases memory/queue pressure on gateway nodes. we need circuit-breakers and backpressure to avoid OOM during bursts. also per-tenant sharding to prevent noisy neighbor.
sophia: if we go agent-heavy, we'll need a lighter-weight config distribution (grpc stream + incremental deltas). we don't want full reloads for tiny policy tweaks.
tom: deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-gateway v1.14 scheduled to canary at 1833470000. :robot_face:
alex: let's list failure modes for each approach quickly:
- gateway fanout: gateway OOM, high egress costs, single control point for policy, easier to hotfix
- agent multiplex: config drift, upgrade complexity, lower egress, better local latency

maya: solid list. for the spike deliverable: i'll prototype a gateway pipeline that can shard tenants across exporter workers and a minimal agent change that does per-tenant tagging + local sampling. aim to demo both with a synthetic noisy tenant.
ian: timeline?
maya: prototype in 3 days, demo next week. if we're aligned on hybrid fallback, i'll design the console wiring for exporter rules — simple rule editor first.
sophia: also add an eval to measure P50/P95 latency and tokenized cost estimate for egress per 1k spans.
tom: i'll draft backpressure knobs for gateway (queue limits, per-tenant token bucket, circuit-breaker metrics).
alex: i'll scope console impact and schema changes for exporter wiring + retention fields.
maya: sweet. if anyone wants to pair on the prototype reach out. i'll push a design doc to the docs repo and ping here. thanks! :thumbsup:
